Your guest is about to leave.
A brand just built a story around **stopping them**.
Maaza is Coca-Cola India’s mango drink. For Diwali it released **“Don’t Go Na”**, its first brand-led micro-drama: **seven episodes** on its Instagram and YouTube channels, made with Ogilvy India.

A young man and woman meet at a Diwali party. A shared Maaza starts a romance that grows through **small gestures, conversations and invitations**. The title borrows what Indian hosts say to a guest heading for the door.

A single film gets watched once. Seven episodes give people **a reason to come back to the page**, and the drink becomes **the spark that starts the story** instead of the voice that interrupts it. The hosting habit is one the audience knows from their own homes.

Series live on **the next episode**. If episode three is less watchable than episode one, viewers drift and the drink is left inside a half-told story. Comments will also **judge the acting** before they judge the mango.

Before you try a series:
-> Pick **one custom** your audience already feels
-> Let the product **start** the story, never narrate it
-> Plan **episode three** before you shoot episode one
Somewhere this Diwali, a guest stands at the door with her bag while her host holds out a glass.
